chains_identified.name: NextAuth.js callbackUrl Open Redirect → Session Hijack
steps: Target /api/auth/signin?callbackUrl= parameter on NextAuth.js Azure AD provider
Victim clicks link, Azure AD OAuth2 flow initiates with legitimate IDP
Upon OAuth completion, NextAuth redirects to unvalidated callbackUrl (attacker domain)
Attacker server receives session token cookie or authorization code in redirect
Replay session token against revops-dev.vercel.app to establish authenticated session
missing_evidence: Confirm callbackUrl parameter accepts external URLs without validation (e.g., test callbackUrl=https://example.com)
Verify NextAuth.js version in use — versions < 4.24.5 have known callbackUrl open redirect (CVE-2023-48309)
Confirm redirect occurs post-OAuth to the attacker-controlled callbackUrl
Determine if session token is transmitted in the redirect (cookie SameSite=None or URL fragment)

supporting_signals: NextAuth.js confirmed as auth framework — historically vulnerable to callbackUrl open redirect
Azure AD OAuth2 only auth path — victim auth flow is predictable and phishable
/api/auth/providers publicly accessible — confirms Azure AD callback URL structure exposed
lesson_0_001: enumerate all provider callback URLs as attack surfaces
Edge e_auth_to_oauth_cb already exists with ev=0.75 as candidate
blocking_signals: NextAuth.js newer versions (>=4.24.5) restrict callbackUrl to same-origin by default
CSRF protections may prevent state parameter tampering
tot_reasoning.ev_justification: Strong structural signal (NextAuth + Azure AD confirmed), known CVE pattern, high-value target (production SaaS). Blocked only by version-specific patching. EV=0.82.

chains_identified.name: Express Backend Route Enumeration → Unauthenticated Data Access (Dev=Prod Container)
steps: Enumerate Express backend API routes: /api, /api/v1, /api/v2, /docs, /swagger, /openapi.json unauthenticated
Probe /health already confirmed returning env:production — signals dev and prod share same container/config
Identify routes lacking auth middleware (missing JWT/session validation)
Issue unauthenticated GET/POST requests to business data endpoints (leads, revenue, pipeline)
Extract CRM/RevOps data: customer records, deal values, pipeline stages
Optionally: probe CORS preflight — if Access-Control-Allow-Origin: * with credentials, enable cross-origin data theft from browser
missing_evidence: CORS preflight capture: Access-Control-Allow-Origin and Access-Control-Allow-Credentials headers (lesson_0_009 high priority)
Confirm dev backend has production data access (env:production response is strong signal but not confirmed data access)
Identify at least one business-logic endpoint missing auth middleware
Azure Container Apps sibling enumeration: other apps in livelystone-c1480484 namespace (lesson_0_003)

supporting_signals: /health confirmed unauthenticated and returns env:production — critical misconfiguration
lesson_0_004 HIGH: dev env with env:production label means dev and prod may share same backend container/config with full production data access
lesson_0_002 HIGH: probe beyond /health — /api, /v1, /docs unauthenticated before assuming full auth protection
lesson_0_009 HIGH: CORS headers present but Allow-Origin not captured — credentials-bearing cross-origin requests may be allowed
Express.js backend confirmed — manual auth middleware patterns are error-prone, common to have route gaps
3 confirmed evidence findings on n_expr_back node
blocking_signals: JWT/session token may be enforced globally via middleware (e.g., express-jwt with unless)
Azure Container Apps may have network-level access controls beyond the application layer
tot_reasoning.ev_justification: Multiple high-priority lessons directly target this chain. env:production disclosure from unauthenticated endpoint is a confirmed finding. CORS misconfiguration is untested but flagged high-priority. EV=0.79.

chains_identified.name: Azure AD OIDC State/Nonce Bypass → Account Takeover
steps: Enumerate Azure AD tenant configuration via /api/auth/providers (publicly accessible)
Extract clientId, tenantId, and authorization endpoint from provider metadata
Test CSRF protection: initiate OAuth flow, capture state parameter, attempt state reuse or fixation
Test nonce validation: attempt token substitution by replaying id_token with modified claims
If state parameter is missing or predictable — forge OAuth callback request with arbitrary code
If nonce is not validated — substitute id_token from a different user/attacker-controlled Azure AD account
Result: authenticate as arbitrary user (account takeover) or bypass authentication entirely
missing_evidence: Capture and analyze state parameter entropy/format during OAuth flow initiation
Verify nonce claim is validated in NextAuth.js Azure AD provider configuration
Test if state parameter can be reused across OAuth sessions (CSRF protection bypass)
Check if NextAuth.js NEXTAUTH_SECRET is properly set — weak or default secrets enable JWT forgery
Determine if multiple Azure AD tenants are accepted or if tenant is locked to a single org

supporting_signals: /api/auth/providers publicly accessible — exposes full OAuth2 configuration including clientId
Azure AD as sole auth provider — OIDC state/nonce bypass would result in full account takeover with no fallback
NextAuth.js NEXTAUTH_SECRET misconfiguration (weak/default) enables JWT session forgery
lesson_0_001: providers endpoint exposed — immediately enumerate all callback URLs as attack surface
Single auth provider means no MFA bypass complexity — one successful bypass = full access
blocking_signals: Azure AD enforces strict redirect_uri validation at the IDP level — callback substitution constrained to registered URIs
NextAuth.js 4.x uses PKCE by default for authorization code flow — reduces token interception risk
Modern NextAuth versions rotate state per-session and validate nonce properly
tot_reasoning.ev_justification: High-value attack if successful (full account takeover), but blocked by Azure AD redirect_uri enforcement and PKCE. Requires active testing to confirm state/nonce weaknesses. EV=0.71.
